title_he: בֵּין יָדֶיךָ הָרַכּוֹת שַׂמְתִּי רֹאשִׁי בְּשָׁלוֹם
review: The hymn is the repose of the beloved: 1:1–4 is Ps 121:3–4 (לֹא־יָנוּם שֹׁמְרֶךָ) with Song 2:6, the chorus is Ps 42:9 with Ps 137:2 (the harp on the willows) and Ps 119:54, 2:1–4 is Ps 55:23 with Ps 94:19, and 3:1–4 is Ps 73:26 with Rom 8:38–39.

The chorus is printed as a block of six lines and the corpus records it as the labelled القرار stanza; the payload keeps six lines, with the harp-and-exile couplet in the middle, as the print sets it.

1:4 תִּרְעֶה חַיַּי וְלֹא תָנוּם — the Arabic تَرْعَى وُجُودِي لَا تَنَام joins the shepherd verb to the unsleeping eye; the Hebrew keeps both with רָעָה and נוּם, because Ps 121:4 is the verse behind the line and its comfort is the wakefulness.
2:4 כַּר־רֹאשִׁי — the Arabic وِسَادَتِي is the pillow; the Hebrew uses כַּר, the cushion-word of 1 Sam 19:13, so the bosom is a physical resting-place and not a figure for comfort.
